journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: The process of forming a decision gives rise to an estimate of its quality or likelihood of success. This graded sense of confidence is important for guiding subsequent decisions, but a neural mechanism linking subjective confidence to formation of the next decision has not been identified. We trained two male rhesus macaques to report a perceptual choice and simultaneous confidence judgment in a reaction-time (RT) motion discrimination task. Monkeys were more likely to repeat a rewarded choice when they reported low confidence on the previous trial, and showed greater changes in RT after a surprising outcome (low-confidence correct or high-confidence error). Neural activity in the lateral intraparietal area (LIP) encoded the previous trial's choice and confidence more strongly after a low-confidence correct trial, and the strength of history encoding was correlated with a trial-by-trial estimate of choice bias. Ramping dynamics of the decoded decision variable also depended systematically on the conjunction of confidence and reward on the previous trial, in a manner that reflected individual differences between animals. The findings suggest that LIP not only reflects the formation of the current decision but could participate in confidence-guided learning via adjustments of the subsequent decision process.Significance statement Decision confidence is of primary interest in the study of metacognition, yet it also plays a key role in learning, serving as a graded prediction of accuracy that modulates the response to feedback. Reanalyzing data from nonhuman primates performing a reaction-time (RT) motion discrimination task with explicit confidence reports, we found that adjustments of choice bias and RT were gated by the animal's self-reported confidence on the previous trial. The interaction of confidence and outcome (reward or punishment) was reflected in the activity of parietal (LIP) neurons on the subsequent trial, in ways largely consistent with the behavioral effects. The results and accompanying computational model suggest plausible functional links between the neuronal substrates of perceptual decision making and reinforcement learning.

title: State and Local Policymakers' Engagement with Neuroscience to Improve Health Policy in the United States.
abstract: Neuroscience is useful for making progress on public health challenges such as mental health, aging, violence, and addiction. State and local policymakers have substantial authority over these issues but do not always have access to the research and counsel they want. To inform initiatives that could bridge the gap, high-quality information on policymakers' existing and desired engagement is needed. We conducted four nationally representative surveys of local elected policymakers, local public sector staff, state legislators, and state public sector staff to gather this information. Across the four samples, 13.8-28.6% reported recently interacting with a neuroscientist, while 50.3-73.6% reported unmet desire to do so. Prior exposure to disseminated neuroscience information varied, from 19.1 to 68.0% across the samples. Unmet desire for neuroscience-related policy briefs (50.5-76.8%) and news articles (52.7-68.9%) were among the most common for all policymakers. Unmet desire crossed party lines, though with some partisan differences. These findings suggest several avenues to increase evidence-informed health policymaking.

title: Dopamine release in the medullary reticular formation is related to locomotor velocity.
abstract: Dopamine is classically recognized for modulating locomotion through basal ganglia circuits. However, it also modulates motor circuits in the brainstem and spinal cord. The medullary reticular formation (MRF) integrates supraspinal motor commands and relays them to the spinal cord, yet the role of dopamine in this region is poorly understood. Using the genetically encoded dopamine sensor dLight1.4, we observed that dopamine release in the MRF decreased during the initiation of locomotion and showed an inverse correlation with locomotor velocity. Dopamine release was also modulated during directional head turns. RNA in situ hybridization revealed D2R mRNA expression is present in about one-third of glutamatergic reticulospinal neurons (RSNs), whereas D4R mRNA expression is nearly absent. Retrograde viral tracing identified the A11 region, encompassing dopaminergic TH+ cells, as the primary source of dopaminergic input to the MRF, with minimal contributions from other dopaminergic nuclei. Anterograde tracing demonstrated that A11 neurons project ipsilaterally throughout the rostrocaudal MRF and form putative synaptic contacts with neuronal populations that project to the spinal cord. These findings reveal discrete dopaminergic projections from the A11 region to the MRF and lead to the hypothesis that the A11-MRF dopaminergic pathway acts as a gain-control mechanism setting the excitability of D2 receptor-expressing reticulospinal neurons, thereby providing state-dependent control of locomotor speed.Significance Statement The medullary reticular formation (MRF) is a critical hub for controlling diverse motor behaviors; however, the source and organization of its dopaminergic inputs remain unclear. Here we identify A11 dopamine neurons as the principal dopaminergic projection to the MRF. Dopamine signaling in the MRF correlates inversely with locomotor velocity and is modulated during ipsilateral head turns. Furthermore, the expression of D2Rs on glutamatergic reticulospinal neurons identifies these cells as primary targets for dopaminergic modulation.

title: Serum neuron-derived extracellular vesicle mitochondrial DNA as a potential biomarker for mild cognitive impairment due to AD.
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represents the initial clinical manifestation, eventually evolving into the distinctive features of Alzheimer's disease (AD), making its early identification crucial. Notably, mitochondrial dysfunction is an early characteristic of AD. Neuron-derived extracellular vesicles (NDEVs) can cross the blood-brain barrier, and their mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) can reflect intracerebral lesions, showing considerable potential. In this study, we investigated the alterations in mtDNA within serum NDEVs and evaluated their potential as early diagnostic biomarkers for MCI due to AD. A total of 42 MCI patients, 49 AD patients, and 57 age-matched cognitively unimpaired (CU) controls were enrolled. Serum NDEVs were enriched and characterized, and their mtDNA levels were quantified by qPCR. ROC curve was used to analyze diagnostic performance, and the integration of multimodal biomarkers was explored. Serum NDEVs mtDNA levels were decreased in patients with AD-MCI, and a significant positive correlation was observed between serum NDEVs mtDNA levels and MMSE scores in MCI patients (r = 0.4864, P = 0.0407), and a similar association was observed in the AD group (r = 0.3857, P = 0.0469). In terms of diagnostic performance, serum NDEV mtDNA demonstrated outstanding discrimination between CU controls and AD subjects, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.965 (95% CI: 0.933-0.997), with 97.92% sensitivity and 89.09% specificity. Moreover, it also demonstrated moderate efficacy in differentiating early MCI from AD (AUC = 0.736, 95% CI: 0.629-0.842; sensitivity = 72.92%, specificity = 66.67%). In exploratory analyses of clinical and metabolic factors, serum NDEV mtDNA levels were positively correlated with HCY in MCI patients, while in AD patients, NDEV mtDNA levels were elevated in those with diabetes and positively correlated with TG. Notably, integrating NDEV mtDNA with established biomarkers, including p-Tau 217, GFAP, and APOE ε4 carrier status, significantly improved the accuracy of MCI detection, highlighting its value in multimodal biomarker strategies. Serum NDEVs mtDNA levels were significantly reduced in patients with MCI and AD, suggesting strong potential as an early diagnostic biomarker for MCI due to AD.

title: Normative functional network localization of gray matter alterations in idiopathic generalized epilepsy.
abstract: Idiopathic generalized epilepsy (IGE) has traditionally been considered a non-lesional epilepsy syndrome on conventional MRI, yet voxel-based morphometry (VBM) studies have reported subtle gray matter (GM) abnormalities across diverse brain regions. These findings remain spatially heterogeneous and difficult to reconcile. We aimed to characterize the normative functional connectivity patterns associated with reported GM alterations in IGE using functional connectivity network mapping (FCNM), and to explore whether these spatially heterogeneous findings show a reproducible pattern of observed network overlap. We systematically identified 18 whole-brain VBM studies of IGE, including 111 reported peak coordinates from 1,492 participants. Coordinates reflecting both increased and decreased GM were pooled in the primary analysis to characterize normative connectivity patterns associated with reported GM alterations irrespective of alteration direction. Using resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data from a normative discovery cohort (Human Connectome Project, N = 1,093), we mapped the functional connectivity of these GM coordinates to identify a convergent IGE-related network. The reproducibility of the observed spatial pattern was explored using an independent, cross-scanner validation cohort (Southwest University Adult Lifespan Dataset, N = 329) and two alternative seed sizes (1-mm and 7-mm radii). Reported GM alterations in IGE were associated with an observed distributed normative functional connectivity pattern involving the bilateral middle temporal gyri, bilateral thalami, left superior frontal gyrus, and right putamen. In the HCP discovery analysis, this network showed the greatest observed overlap with the subcortical network (overlap proportion = 42.77%) and secondary correspondence with the default mode network (DMN; overlap proportion = 11.06%). Analysis using the independent SALD connectome showed a similar descriptive pattern, with the greatest observed overlap again involving the subcortical network (overlap proportion = 43.98%), whereas DMN correspondence was weaker. Reported GM alterations in IGE converge most robustly onto a subcortical normative functional network involving the thalamus and putamen, with additional DMN involvement observed primarily in the HCP discovery analysis. These findings provide preliminary, descriptive evidence that reported GM alterations in IGE are associated with a reproducible subcortical normative connectivity pattern across two connectome datasets, although the available analyses do not establish above-chance or disease-specific network convergence.

title: LGALS3BP is associated with selective cargo enrichment in neuroblastoma extracellular vesicles.
abstract: LGALS3BP (also known as Galectin-3-binding protein, Gal-3BP, or 90 K) is a multifunctional secreted glycoprotein involved in tumor progression and has emerged as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in several malignancies, including neuroblastoma (NB). Increasing evidence suggests that LGALS3BP contributes to shaping the NB tumor microenvironment (TME), particularly through its enrichment on tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), where it may regulate tumor-stroma interplay. We investigated whether LGALS3BP contributes to stromal cell modulation in NB and is associated with changes in EV cargo composition. A patient-derived NB cell line naturally lacking LGALS3BP (hNB CTRL) and a matched counterpart ectopically re-expressing LGALS3BP (hNB LGALS3BP) were used. Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMMSCs) were exposed to NB-derived conditioned media (CM) to assess cytokine secretion and LGALS3BP detection in recipient cells. EV cargo was analyzed by microRNA (miRNA) and proteomic profiling. Selected candidates were validated by qPCR and immunoblotting on NB-derived EVs. LGALS3BP-containing CM was associated with an altered BMMSCs secretory profile, while tumor-derived extracellular LGALS3BP was detected in BMMSCs. Seven miRNAs were enriched in LGALS3BP-EVs and reduced in donor cells; four were increased in BMMSCs following EV exposure. Proteomic analysis revealed enrichment of RNA-binding proteins, including SRSF1, in LGALS3BP-EVs. LGALS3BP is associated with altered EV cargo composition and BMMSCs secretory responses, potentially contributing to tumor-stroma communication within the NB TME.

title: Morinda Officinalis Oligosaccharides Alleviate Post-Stroke Depression-Like Behaviors Alongside Increased Gut Microbial Diversity and Butyrate Levels and Reduced Hippocampal Pla2g4a Expression.
abstract: Post-stroke depression (PSD) represents a common and debilitating complication after cerebral ischemia, yet mechanism-based therapies remain an urgent unmet need. The microbiota-gut-brain axis has been implicated in PSD pathophysiology, but the precise molecular pathways are largely elusive. Morinda officinalis oligosaccharides (MOO), a clinically approved antidepressant in China, exhibit poor oral absorption, raising the possibility of a gut-dependent mechanism. Male C57BL/6J mice were subjected to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) followed by 21 days of chronic restraint stress (CRS) to establish a PSD model. MOO (50 mg/kg/day) was administered via gavage from Day 7 to 27. Depression-like behaviors, 16S rRNA-based gut microbiota profiling, short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) quantification, intestinal and blood-brain barrier integrity assessments, and hippocampal proteomics were performed. The transferability of MOO-associated fecal effects was assessed using a donor-controlled fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) design. The butyrate-Pla2g4a relationship was further examined by sodium butyrate supplementation and AAV-mediated hippocampal Pla2g4a overexpression. MOO administration altered gut microbial composition, increased the abundance of probiotics and decreased the abundance of harmful bacteria, and was accompanied by increased fecal butyrate levels. The donor-controlled FMT experiment provided preliminary evidence that fecally transferable factors from MOO-treated PSD donors may contribute to behavioral improvements in PSD recipients. MOO and sodium butyrate treatment were associated with improved indices of intestinal and blood-brain barrier integrity. Hippocampal proteomics identified Pla2g4a, a phospholipase linked to neuroinflammation, as a candidate molecule related to the observed effects. Both MOO and sodium butyrate treatment were associated with reduced hippocampal Pla2g4a expression, and Pla2g4a expression was inversely correlated with butyrate levels. Hippocampal Pla2g4a overexpression attenuated the behavioral improvements associated with sodium butyrate treatment, supporting the functional involvement of Pla2g4a in the response to sodium butyrate. MOO treatment was associated with improved depression-like behaviors in PSD mice, accompanied by gut microbial alterations, increased fecal butyrate, improved barrier integrity, and reduced hippocampal Pla2g4a expression. FMT findings provided preliminary evidence that fecally transferable factors from MOO-treated donors may contribute to behavioral improvements, while Pla2g4a overexpression attenuated the behavioral effects of sodium butyrate. These findings highlight a potential association among MOO, gut-derived butyrate, barrier integrity, and hippocampal Pla2g4a in PSD.

title: STRAND: a comprehensive subcellular-resolved spatial transcriptome RNA architecture and navigation database.
abstract: Subcellular RNA localization serves as a critical regulatory layer governing cellular polarization, local translation, and functional compartmentalization. Recent advances in high-resolution spatial transcriptomics have provided unprecedented opportunities to resolve these intracellular architectures at single-molecule resolution. However, relevant datasets are dispersed across studies and repositories, vary substantially in processing procedures and standards, severely limiting their cross-study reuse. To bridge this gap, we present STRAND (Subcellular-Resolved Spatial Transcriptome RNA Architecture and Navigation Database), a curated data resource and analysis platform for the automated harvesting, quality control, and interpretation of subcellular spatial transcriptomics data. Through an agent-assisted curation pipeline, STRAND has assembled 35 subcellular-resolution datasets from six major platforms, covering 17 tissue types in human and mouse and totalling ∼4.9 billion transcript coordinates. Building upon this standardized data resource, STRAND provides an analytical workflow spanning cell segmentation evaluation, cell-type annotation, RNA localization/colocalization pattern annotation, and subcellular compartment inference. Two case studies demonstrate that STRAND successfully identifies established RNA localization patterns in cultured cell lines and detects drug-induced RNA relocalization in cardiomyocytes. STRAND is openly available at https://strand.phasep.pro.

title: dictyBase 2026: a reimplementation of the Dictyostelium model organism database on minimal infrastructure.
abstract: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Many of its genes have human orthologs implicated in disease, making it a useful model organism for studying conditions ranging from cancer to neurodegeneration. dictyBase has served this community for two decades as a home for genomic data, protocols, a stock center, and community news. Here we describe a complete reimplementation of dictyBase as a self-contained service that uses static data files rather than a database server. Each gene record gathers curated function, human-disease context, developmental expression, and protein structure in a single webpage. The site also provides tools for sequence search, genome browsing, enrichment analysis, and experimental design. The complete Dicty Stock Center catalog of 7055 strains and 1265 plasmids is included, and both can be ordered from the site. New literature is curated by an author-in-the-loop pipeline. A language model drafts the annotations, the authors of the paper correct them, and a curator approves them. Analyses can be run on curator-approved annotations alone or extended to include those still awaiting review. dictyBase is freely available at https://dicty.org.

title: Electrophysiological properties of mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive.
abstract: The neocortex has the largest volume, whereas the cerebellum houses the most neurons of the mammalian brain, underscoring paramount functions for interactions between them. Neocortical projections to the cerebellum involve both the mossy fibre and climbing fibre systems; mossy fibres find their origin predominantly in the pons, whereas the climbing fibres are relayed via subnuclei of the inferior olive (IO) that receive cortical input via the mesodiencephalic junction (MDJ). Given that climbing fibres regulate cerebellar plasticity in a timing-dependent manner, the MDJ-IO pathway probably contributes to both sensorimotor and cognitive learning. However, the physiological properties of IO-projecting MDJ neurons remain largely unknown. Here, we made targeted whole-cell recordings in brain slices of the mouse MDJ, separating IO- from non-IO-projecting neurons following retrograde tracing. We show that IO-projecting neurons are, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, highly spontaneously active and capable of high-frequency bursts of ≤350 Hz during current injections. Optogenetic stimulation shows that excitatory neocortical inputs to IO-projecting MDJ neurons can be integrated directly with excitatory inputs from the cerebellar nuclei. Moreover, unlike non-IO-projecting neurons, IO-projecting MDJ neurons depolarize and repolarize quickly, and hyperpolarizing inputs consistently trigger rebound action potentials upon stimulus offset. This hyperpolarization is probably induced predominantly by inhibitory inputs from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey, which provide prominent bilateral inputs to MDJ neurons, as revealed by viral tracing in Gad2-Cre mice. Our results highlight how neocortical inputs to the MDJ can be transformed into diverse IO firing patterns and thereby contribute to the required specifics of cerebellar learning. KEY POINTS: The mesodiencephalic junction is an important brainstem region connecting the cerebral cortex with the cerebellum through its projection to the inferior olive, the sole source of the climbing fibres that drive cerebellar learning. We find that mesodiencephalic junction neurons projecting to the inferior olive represent a population of physiologically distinct neurons, capable of high firing frequencies and rebound activity following hyperpolarization. We reveal that mesodiencephalic junction neurons receive prominent excitatory inputs from neocortex and cerebellar nuclei, whereas their main inhibitory inputs are derived from the ventral tegmental area and periaqueductal grey. These findings shed light on how the activity of neurons in the mesodiencephalic junction can be regulated and how these neurons might influence activity in the inferior olive, and thereby cerebellar learning.

title: Apigenin and Placental β-Endorphin Signaling: A Hypothesis-Generating Mechanistic Review.
journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
abstract: The placenta functions as a dynamic endocrine hub that translates maternal exposures into offspring developmental programming, consistent with the Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) framework. Beta-endorphin (β-EP), a placental POMC-derived opioid peptide, signals through MOR/DOR/KOR receptors to regulate angiogenesis, immune tolerance, oxidative stress, inflammation, and nutrient transport. Apigenin, a dietary flavone found in parsley, chamomile, and celery, modulates several pathways that overlap with this axis, including CREB/PKA signaling, DNA methyltransferase activity, Nrf2, NF-κB/NLRP3, and Foxp3+ Treg differentiation, although most supporting evidence derives from non-placental systems such as cancer lines, keratinocytes, and macrophages. This review proposes that apigenin may amplify placental β-EP signaling across three conceptual tiers: a biosynthetic tier involving CREB/PKA-mediated POMC activation and 11β-HSD1 inhibition; a receptor-level tier involving DNMT1/3a inhibition and OPRM1 demethylation; and an effector-level tier involving Nrf2 activation, NF-κB/NLRP3 suppression, and Treg expansion, the last representing the strongest trophoblast-level evidence. Given reported β-EP dysregulation in preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, and intrauterine growth restriction, apigenin's relevance to these disorders remains an untested hypothesis rather than a validated therapeutic strategy, informed by a structured, non-systematic literature search (1986-2026).
keywords: Developmental Origins of Health and Disease

title: Retronasal olfactory recovery during biologic therapy for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: a prospective longitudinal study with parallel orthonasal assessment.
abstract: Olfactory dysfunction is a key feature of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP). While biologics improve orthonasal olfaction, longitudinal data on retronasal function and differences between inflammatory targets remain limited. This study evaluated retronasal olfactory recovery over time during biologic therapy and compared IL-4/IL-13 versus IL-5 pathway blockade. In this prospective longitudinal study, adults with severe CRSwNP starting biologics were assessed at baseline and after 4, 12, and 24 weeks. Orthonasal olfaction was measured using Sniffin' Sticks (TDI), and retronasal function with a validated 20-item identification test. Clinical outcomes included nasal polyp score (NPS), peak nasal inspiratory flow, and SNOT-22. Repeated-measures ANOVA was used to evaluate longitudinal changes and time-by-treatment interactions. Sixty-nine patients were included (44 dupilumab, 25 mepolizumab). At baseline, mean TDI was 15.0 and retronasal score 7.2, indicating severe impairment. All outcomes improved significantly over time. Retronasal function improved rapidly within 4 weeks (7.2 to 10.4). TDI increased progressively (15.0 to 26.0 at 24 weeks). Significant time-by-treatment interactions were observed for retronasal identification, TDI, SNOT-22, and NPS, indicating non-parallel recovery patterns with dupilumab being associated with greater improvements in retronasal function and symptoms compared with mepolizumab. Biologic therapy leads to substantial recovery of both retronasal and orthonasal olfaction in CRSwNP, with distinct considetemporal dynamics. Retronasal function shows rapid improvement and may be particularly sensitive to IL-4/IL-13 blockade, supporting its potential role as an early functional marker of response to biologic therapy.

title: Spatiotemporal Remodeling of Neural Excitability Following Ischemic Stroke: Regional Mechanisms From the Infarct Core to Brainstem-Spinal Output Systems: A Structured Narrative Review.
abstract: Changes in neural excitability after ischemic stroke affect lesion growth, recovery of function, and long-term motor problems. People often think of these changes as just an increase or decrease in neural activity. This view does not explain why excitability changes are different at different stages, brain regions, or mechanisms. It also does not explain why these changes can cause injury, help recovery, or lead to maladaptation. In the acute phase, the main areas involved are the infarct core and the ischemic penumbra. Here, excitability problems include membrane instability, prolonged depolarization, spreading depolarizations (SDs), changes in the fluid environment, and abnormal neurovascular responses. These problems together create harmful excitability that makes the lesion bigger. In the subacute phase, the dominant substrates shift toward the peri-infarct cortex, ipsilesional primary motor cortex, and bilateral sensorimotor networks. Here, excitability changes are defined by excitatory-inhibitory rebalancing, reduction of excessive tonic inhibition, restoration of cortical responsiveness, and experience-dependent network reorganization, forming restorative excitability that supports neural plasticity and functional recovery. During the subacute phase, excitatory-inhibitory rebalancing becomes a key synaptic mechanism of recovery, involving glutamatergic transmission, γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)ergic tonic and phasic inhibition, synaptic scaling, dendritic remodeling, and activity-dependent refinement of surviving peri-infarct circuits. In the chronic phase, in a subset of patients, the dominant substrates further shift toward the brainstem-spinal output system, where compensatory recruitment of alternative descending pathways may contribute to abnormal synergies, spasticity, and low-resolution motor control, representing maladaptive hyperexcitability. We therefore argue that poststroke excitability should not be interpreted within a static high-/low-excitability dichotomy but defined by when it occurs, where it is expressed, and at which mechanistic level it predominates.

title: AAV-mediated Modulation of Dorsal Raphe Serotonergic Neurons Recapitulates Fenfluramine Efficacy in a Rat Model of Dravet Syndrome.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
abstract: Dravet Syndrome (DS) is a catastrophic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) primarily caused by SCN1A haploinsufficiency. It is characterized by refractory hyperthermia-induced seizures, neurodevelopmental delay, and an elevated risk of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) compared to other childhood epilepsies. While the small molecule fenfluramine (FFA) provides profound clinical benefit, its potential for systemic side effects and a poorly defined mechanism of action (MOA) underscores the need for more targeted interventions. Using a Scn1a+/- rat model of DS, we demonstrate that chronic FFA treatment reduces the frequency of hyperthermia-induced seizures and attenuates pathological EEG network hypersynchrony. Furthermore, FFA administration ameliorates hyperactivity and depressive-like comorbidities, an effect associated with a marked reduction in hippocampal neuroinflammation and microglial overactivation. Transcriptomic analysis implicated serotonergic signaling in the therapeutic response to FFA, and subsequent anatomical and functional analyses revealed enhanced activity of dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) serotonergic neurons following FFA treatment. Cell-type-specific AAV-mediated modulation of DRN serotonergic neurons was sufficient to reproduce the key antiseizure and electrophysiological effects of FFA. Together, our findings identify the DRN serotonergic circuit as a therapeutically relevant circuit and provide proof-of-concept for mechanism-driven, circuit-specific neuromodulation strategies for Dravet syndrome.

title: A Damage-Gated Small-Molecule Chimera Selectively Enhances Mitophagy by Coupling Dysfunctional Mitochondria to Autophagy.
abstract: Mitophagy is a central mitochondrial quality-control pathway, and its pharmacological activation is considered to be geroprotective. However, its small-molecule activators act indirectly by perturbing metabolism or mitochondrial function, limiting selectivity and increasing toxicity. Here, we describe a chemical biology strategy for activating damage-responsive mitophagy using bifunctional small molecules that couple mitochondrial recognition to the recruitment of the autophagic machinery. We designed and synthesized a focused library of chimeric molecules and identified MG-1 as a lead compound. It had minimal effects on basal autophagy but markedly enhanced autophagic flux and mitochondrial clearance under conditions of mitochondrial stress. Biochemical analyses, together with fluorescence and electron microscopy, showed that MG-1 promotes lysosomal degradation of damaged mitochondria without acting as a direct mitochondrial uncoupler. MG-1 was well tolerated across experimental systems and improved locomotor performance in a zebrafish model of MPTP-induced mitochondrial dysfunction. These findings establish damage-gated small-molecule chimeras as a promising approach for selective control of mitochondrial quality.

title: Fuyuan Huoxue Decoction Promotes Lumbar Interbody Fusion in Rats: Role of Macrophage-Driven Inflammation and the TLR9/NF-κB Pathway.
abstract: Delayed union and pseudarthrosis remain complications of lumbar interbody fusion. We investigated Fuyuan Huoxue decoction (FY) in a rat extreme lateral interbody fusion model. FY improved bone mineral density and trabecular architecture. Reduced inflammatory macrophage infiltration and nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) activation at 4 weeks were accompanied by improved bony bridging at 8 weeks. Transcriptomic and network analyses nominated Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9)/NF-κB signaling for functional investigation. FY-medicated serum reduced macrophage inflammatory markers and extracellular double-stranded DNA (dsDNA), promoted bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) osteogenesis, and attenuated impairment induced by inflammatory macrophage-conditioned medium. DNase treatment reduced this medium's inhibitory effects, whereas a separate exogenous dsDNA challenge impaired osteogenesis and was attenuated by a TLR9 antagonist. TLR9 agonist and antagonist experiments in BMSCs and a 2-week in vivo agonist intervention supported pathway involvement. Human nonunion single-cell data showed increased phospholipid scramblase 1 and interleukin-6 expression in myeloid cells. These findings support complementary pro-osteogenic and anti-inflammatory actions of FY and identify TLR9/NF-κB as a candidate pathway contributing to fusion repair.

title: Stakeholder Perspectives and Perceived Usability of an AI-Enabled Stroke Rehabilitation Platform: A Multicentre Mixed-Methods Focus Group Study With Stroke Survivors, Caregivers, and Clinicians.
journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
abstract: AI-enabled digital neurorehabilitation may support home-based stroke recovery, but its adoption depends on user acceptance. Within the European AISN project (Integrating Artificial Intelligence in Stroke Neurorehabilitation), we explored how stroke survivors, caregivers and healthcare professionals perceived the usability of a preliminary version of an AI-based rehabilitation platform, and the barriers to its adoption. We conducted a convergent parallel mixed-methods study in four European countries (Spain, Italy, France and Romania). Seventeen focus groups combined hands-on testing of the platform components (RGS ecosystem and MIMS dashboard) with semi-structured discussions. Usability was measured with the System Usability Scale (SUS), using exploratory analyses: stroke survivors and caregivers rated the RGS, whereas healthcare professionals rated the combined MIMS/RGS system. Qualitative data were analysed thematically and integrated with SUS total and item scores in a joint display. Seventy-one participants took part (27 stroke survivors, 17 caregivers, and 27 healthcare professionals). The mean SUS score was 68.1 ± 16.0 (grade C). Stroke survivors rated the patient interface (RGS) lower than caregivers rating the same interface (58.9 ± 16.5 vs. 75.6 ± 13.3; p = 0.002); professionals, who rated the clinician-facing components (RGS/MIMS) after a demonstration, scored 72.7 ± 12.8. Six themes emerged: ease of use and clinical utility, personalised treatment and feedback, technical reliability and trust, the digital literacy divide, the need for human mediation and workflow and socio-economic integration. Patients' concerns about reliability converged with their lower confidence in using the system (SUS item 9), whereas digital literacy, although described as a major barrier, was not associated with patients' scores. Human mediation, clinician time and reimbursement emerged as barriers not captured by the SUS. Autonomous home use does not yet appear realistic for stroke survivors without support. All stakeholder groups favoured a hybrid model combining AI-driven exercise delivery with clinician oversight. These findings are informing the refinement of the AISN platform and the design of a forthcoming randomised controlled trial. Stroke survivors (n = 27), formal and informal caregivers (n = 17), and multidisciplinary healthcare professionals (n = 27) participated in this study as relevant stakeholders. Their contribution was central to the formative evaluation of the AISN platform, including hands-on testing and discussion sessions focused on the RGS ecosystem and MIMS dashboard. Patients and caregivers contributed their lived experiences, expectations, concerns, and priorities regarding AI-assisted home rehabilitation, while healthcare professionals provided their clinical expertise, including perspectives on clinical utility and workflow integration. Stakeholders were not involved in the conceptual design of the focus group (FG) study protocol, the systematic analysis of the qualitative data, or the drafting and dissemination of the manuscript. Nevertheless, their feedback served as a cornerstone of the iterative development of the AISN system. The insights and themes identified through their contributions are directly informing final technical refinements to the AISN system architecture and the protocol design for the upcoming randomised controlled trial (RCT), helping to ensure that end-user perspectives are incorporated into the final clinical solution. While the FG script was not formally piloted with a Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement (PPIE) group, it was reviewed through multidisciplinary workshops to ensure language accessibility and clinical safety. Formal PPIE was therefore not implemented as a separate research partnership activity because stakeholders were recruited primarily as participants in a formative usability evaluation, with their experiential and professional perspectives collected as study data rather than as contributions to research design, analysis, or manuscript preparation.

title: A Novel Bioactive Component, Efoba, From Aged Garlic Targets CTSC to Suppress NET-Driven Neuroinflammation and Ameliorate Secondary Brain Injury After Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a devastating neurological disorder with high mortality and disability, where neuroinflammation-driven secondary brain injury is a key pathological hallmark. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) serve as critical pathogenic mediators that amplify neuroinflammation, disrupt blood-brain barrier integrity, and exacerbate brain damage after ICH. This study identifies Efoba, a novel bioactive monomer from aged garlic, and establishes a scalable total‑synthesis route for hundred‑gram‑scale high‑purity production, overcoming low‑yield and supply‑limiting bottlenecks for natural product research. In vivo and in vitro experiments show Efoba markedly ameliorates ICH‑induced neurological impairments and inhibits NET formation. Integrative analyses (Lip-MS, virtual screening, proteomics, transcriptomics) identified cathepsin C (CTSC) as the direct binding target of Efoba. Efoba stabilizes microglial lysosomal membranes, inhibits CTSC release, blocks NET generation, and exerts neuroprotection against NETs-driven neuroinflammation. CTSC knockout and CTSC overexpression assays further confirm the indispensable role of CTSC in mediating Efoba's neuroprotective and anti‑inflammatory activities. Collectively, this work demonstrates for the first time that Efoba targets CTSC to suppress NET-mediated neuroinflammation, highlighting its therapeutic potential and the translational value of natural active components.

title: Regional Histological Anatomy of the Supraperiosteal Tissues of the Oral Cavity: Implications for Periodontal Flap Surgery and Periosteal Releasing Incisions.
abstract: Periodontal and implant procedures increasingly involve tissue planes superficial to the periosteum, yet their regional anatomy remains poorly understood. This study conducted a histological investigation of the supraperiosteal anatomy of the oral cavity and its implications for periosteal releasing incisions (PRIs). Intraoral dissection of the mimetic muscle was performed using a fresh anatomical donor. Subsequently, maxillary and mandibular incisor, premolar, and molar regions from five formalin-fixed donors were examined histologically using Masson's trichrome staining. Muscular, neural, vascular, and connective tissue structures within 5 mm of the facial alveolar bone surface were evaluated. Supraperiosteal tissue architecture differed markedly by region. Muscular, neural, and vascular structures showed distinct region-specific distributions. The mental nerve and its branches were identified in the mandibular premolar region, whereas facial and buccal vessels were present near the bone surface in the posterior regions. Muscle attachment and intervening connective tissue also varied regionally. Structures potentially injured during PRI and their associated risks are region-dependent. PRI should therefore be guided by region-specific anatomy and the tissues requiring release for sufficient flap mobility rather than by a predetermined incision depth alone.

title: CBD-Rich Does Not Mean THC-Free: A Pediatric Safety Concern.
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research

title: A National Survey of Simulation Use, Limitations, and Future Directions in Neurocritical Care Fellowship Training.
abstract: Details regarding the use and implementation of simulation-based medical education (SBME) among neurocritical care fellowship programs are limited. The objective of this study was to describe the current use of SBME in neurocritical care fellowship education and to assess perceived barriers to SBME growth in both programs currently using simulation and those that are not. We surveyed neurocritical care fellowship program directors using email addresses listed in the San Francisco Match directory using a Qualtrics-based survey platform. Survey questions addressed current utilization of SBME and barriers to SBME growth. Thirty-nine of 72 (54%) program directors responded to our survey. Of the respondents, 95% (37/39) report using SBME in their neurocritical care fellowship training programs. Most (94%, 34/36) programs create their own simulation cases. SBME was most frequently used for trainee education and trainee assessment, and rarely used for quality improvement. The most reported SBME case topics included fundamentals in neurocritical care, vascular neurology, serious illness communication, and interprofessional team dynamics. Simulations rarely focused on headache management or neuro-infectious disease, and simulations on healthcare disparities and implicit bias were not reported among survey respondents. Eighty-two percent (32/39) of responding institutions reported wanting to increase the amount of simulation training offered. Reported barriers include faculty protected time, funding, and mentorship. SBME has been embraced by most responding programs; however, the content of simulation curricula varies. Fellowship directors report interest in expanding SBME at their institutions, though are commonly limited by faculty time constraints, financial support, and mentorship. Future collaboration across institutions and application of SBME in learner assessment and quality improvement may improve simulation growth and innovation in neurocritical care fellowship training.

title: An ESIPT Fluorescent Probe for Detection of Biothiols and H2S: Application in Water Samples, Food Spoilage, and Cell Imaging.
journal: Luminescence : the journal of biological and chemical luminescence
abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S), cysteine (Cys) and glutathione (GSH) are essential for maintaining physiological homeostasis and serve as key biomarkers for disease diagnosis. In this work, six fluorescent probes relying on the ESIPT mechanism were developed for the detection of biothiols and H2S. Specifically, probe AHB-2A demonstrated high sensitivity (LOD: 79 nM), a large Stokes shift (113 nm), and a 66-fold increase in fluorescence at 493 nm. The high sensitivity of AHB-2A enables effective real-time detection of biothiols and H2S in biological applications. In addition, AHB-2A was used to measure H2S in water samples and to monitor the spoilage of food. Furthermore, AHB-2A was capable of imaging both endogenous and exogenous Cys, GSH, and H2S in living cells and exhibited low toxicity in cells treated with high concentrations of the probe. The design strategy highlights both the compound's intrinsic properties and its adaptability to reactive conditions across different application contexts.

title: Glioblastoma as a dynamic tumor ecosystem: from molecular alterations to therapeutic translation.
abstract: For more than a century after its initial description, glioblastoma (GBM) has remained one of the most therapeutically refractory human malignancies, resembling an almost impregnable fortress against modern oncology. Despite extensive molecular characterization and identification of numerous actionable targets, survival outcomes have improved only marginally. GBM is characterized by profound spatial and cellular heterogeneity, adaptive signaling rewiring, extensive phenotypic plasticity, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and major pharmacological constraints imposed by the blood-brain barrier. This review examines the resulting disconnect between biological rationale and clinical outcome through three interrelated translational principles that determine whether mechanistically compelling therapies can achieve meaningful clinical benefit in GBM. First, who is treated and what is biologically active: therapeutic efficacy depends on matching patients to functional pathway dependencies beyond static molecular alterations. Second, whether the drug reaches and modulates its intended target: candidate therapies must achieve sufficient intratumoral exposure and demonstrate target modulation. Third, how the tumor adapts under therapeutic pressure: durable efficacy requires accounting for receptor tyrosine kinase switching, phenotypic plasticity, immune adaptation, and spatial escape. By linking these principles to the molecular, spatial, and pharmacological organization of GBM, this review frames the disease as a dynamic tumor ecosystem and provides a framework for interpreting recurrent clinical failure and guiding more biologically informed therapeutic development.

title: The pathological roles of intrinsically disordered proteins in lysosomal acidification dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and Parkinson's disease (PD) are characterized by the accumulation of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), including amyloid-β (Aβ), tau, and α-synuclein (αSyn). These proteins disrupt neuronal homeostasis through toxic aggregation, impaired proteostasis, and progressive neurodegeneration, in part via dysfunction of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway (ALP). A central feature of this impairment is defective vacuolar-type (H+)-ATPase (V-ATPase) function, leading to lysosomal deacidification and reduced degradative capacity. Pathological IDP species converge on V-ATPase through direct interactions with its subunits or by perturbing its assembly, while also exerting protein-specific effects, including lysosomal membrane destabilization, impaired hydrolase activity, and disrupted endolysosomal trafficking. These combined mechanisms create a reciprocal relationship between lysosomal dysfunction and IDP accumulation, in which impaired lysosomal degradation further promotes the persistence and aggregation of pathological IDP species. This review synthesizes current insights into the molecular interplay between IDPs and lysosomal acidification across AD, FTD, and PD, and highlights how these processes contribute to disease progression. We further discuss emerging therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring lysosomal function. These findings underscore lysosomal dysfunction as a common feature of IDP-driven neurodegeneration and a potential therapeutic target across these disorders.

title: The influence of blueberry (Vaccinium myrtillus) leaf extract on peroxisomal function in microglial cells.
abstract: The presented study investigated possible antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties of Vaccinium myrtillus (VM) extract in murine BV-2 microglial cells, including both wild-type (Wt) and Acyl-CoA oxidase 1-deficient (Acox1-/-) cell lines. The radical scavenging activity was assessed by DPPH assay. The MTT test was used assess the cell viability. Nitric oxide production by cells was quantified by Griess reagent. Catalase activity was evaluated by photometric measurement of the H2O2 decomposition. The measurement of ACOX1 activity was performed using a fluorometry-based assay. Immunoblotting and RT-qPCR techniques were employed to measure protein expression and gene transcription in treated cells. Statistical analysis was conducted using GraphPad Prism, with significance determined at p < 0.05. Radical scavenging activity test assessed the yielded an IC50 value 0.03613 mg/mL, prompting further functional investigations. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation reduced ACOX1 enzymatic activity by approximately 40% in Wt cells. Co-treatment with VM extract restored the activity to initial levels. LPS exposure increased catalase activity and mRNA expression by 1.5-fold each in Wt cells and 2-fold and 4-fold, respectively, in mutant Acox1-/- cells. VM treatment normalized these parameters in Wt cells and significantly attenuated them by about 20% in mutant cells. In addition, the extract also modulated Abcd1 mRNA expression, a gene involved in fatty acid transport into peroxisomes, suggesting a significant influence on cellular peroxisomal lipid handling and redox balance. LPS markedly induced some inflammatory markers, with iNos mRNA and Nitric oxide (NO) levels, increasing up to ~10-fold and ~20-fold, respectively, in Acox1-/- cells. Similarly, Il-1β and Tnf-α mRNA levels were induced by approximately 4 to 30-fold in Wt cells and more than 180- fold in mutant cells. VM extract significantly reduced LPS-induced NO production and downregulated iNos, Tnf-α, and Il-1β mRNA expression in both cell lines. Overall, our findings demonstrate that V. myrtillus extract suppresses the oxidative-stress induced elevated levels of inflammatory markers and probably modulate peroxisomal metabolism. Although the precise molecular mechanisms remain to be clarified, the data support further investigation into the role of peroxisomal lipid metabolism in mediating the biological effects of this extract.

title: Targeting tetrahydrobiopterin metabolism in diabetic neuropathic pain: mechanisms, implications, and therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Diabetic neuropathic pain (DNP) is a debilitating complication affecting up to 50% of diabetic patients and severely impairing their quality of life. Current treatments provide limited relief and carry considerable side effects, underscoring the urgent need for novel, mechanism-based analgesics. Recent studies have identified tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) as a crucial modulator of pain sensitivity. After nerve injury, its levels surge in injured neurons and infiltrating immune cells, amplifying pain signals via nitric oxide (NO) production, neuroinflammation, and ion channel sensitisation. This review addresses the critical translational challenge posed by the BH4 paradox in DNP: although systemic BH4 is essential for vascular and metabolic integrity and is depleted under chronic hyperglycaemia, its localised overproduction in the nervous system drives neuropathic hypersensitivity. Non-selective inhibition of the key upstream enzyme, GTP cyclohydrolase-1 (GCH1), risks systemic BH4 deficiency, impairing neurotransmitter biosynthesis and causing severe vascular and metabolic side effects. Attention has therefore turned to sepiapterin reductase (SPR), the terminal enzyme in BH4 de novo biosynthesis, as a more selective and safer target. SPR inhibition suppresses pathological BH4 overproduction in nociceptive and immune tissues while preserving physiological levels through the dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR)-mediated salvage pathway. Preclinical studies of SPR inhibitors such as sulfasalazine show analgesia with limited central nervous system side effects due to their restricted blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability. To guide clinical application, we synthesise the biochemical, genetic, and physiological roles of BH4 in DNP, and propose a translational biomarker framework for monitoring target engagement and systemic safety in future clinical trials. We outline the mechanistic rationale and translational considerations for developing highly selective SPR inhibitors as a potentially better-tolerated, more selective approach for DNP and other BH4-driven chronic pain conditions. This rationale currently rests largely on genetic, preclinical, and surrogate-biomarker evidence, and no completed human trial has evaluated SPR inhibition for chronic pain. The proposed biomarker framework is therefore intended to inform trial design and dose optimisation rather than to imply current clinical readiness, as one step toward a future precision-medicine strategy for pain.

title: Bioengineered microtissue model of the human nigrostriatal pathway featuring centimeter-scale axon tracts and structural maturation over 6 months in vitro.
abstract: The basal ganglia (BG) comprise a critical neural system involved in voluntary motor coordination and balance. While small animal models have been useful to improve our basic understanding of the development and function of neural systems, they are relatively low-throughput, lack human-specific genomic and target specificity, and fail to recapitulate critical anatomical features such as centimeter-scale axon tracts. Accordingly, bioengineered models replicating human systems-level features such as neuronal constituents, neurophysiology, and long-distance connectivity would be valuable to study BG circuit development, maturation, and function, as well as responses to neurotrauma and neurodegenerative diseases. To address this unmet need, we report the fabrication of a three-dimensional tissue engineered nigrostriatal pathway (TE-NSP) featuring human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) derived dopaminergic (DA) neurons and centimeter-scale axon tracts that were maintained as a long-term in vitro model of key components of BG circuitry. TE-NSPs were fabricated using hyaluronic acid hydrogel microcolumns filled with collagen-laminin solution that were used to seed two types of neuronal aggregates, namely, human iPSC-derived DA and striatal neurons. These TE-NSPs featuring the co-culture of DA and striatal neurons were characterized for phenotypic stability, axonal growth, synaptic integration, and viability over 6 months in vitro. Our results demonstrate anatomically-relevant 3 cm long TE-NSPs with discrete 3D compartmentalized structures connected via > 2 cm long dopaminergic axon tracts. The TE-NSPs exhibited survival up to 6 months in vitro with dense TH + axon tracts and high cell viability. Immunohistochemistry revealed the widespread expression of mature synaptic markers within the TE-NSPs at 180 days in vitro featuring similarity with native in vivo rat striatal tissue. These long-lived TE-NSPs showed robust axonal outgrowth and innervation within the striatal compartment of the engineered tissue. We have established a mature living human iPSC-derived neural microtissue that recapitulates human-relevant anatomical connections and models a key component of the BG circuitry. This bioengineered human microtissue model could serve as a powerful platform for studying neural systems development, function, and neurodegenerative sequelae such as Parkinson's disease, while also providing the basis for an implantable microtissue for circuit-level reconstruction following neurotrauma or neurodegenerative disease.

title: Characteristic central nervous system fingerprints and related molecular signatures in difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis.
abstract: Despite guideline-recommended treatment, approximately 30% of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients remain symptomatic and are classified as difficult-to-treat (D2T), representing an unmet clinical need. D2T RA is a heterogeneous state potentially involving differences across several biological and psychological levels, but the exact underlying mechanisms remain unclear. To capture this complexity, our multimodal cross-sectional study aimed to characterize the contributing factors of the D2T state with a multimodal approach. 31 D2T RA (defined by EULAR, 2021), 18 non-D2T RA patients, and 32 healthy controls (HCs) were included. All participants underwent a clinical assessment, psychological analysis (in-depth interviews, the Rorschach test, and questionnaires), two resting-state functional MRI (fMRI) scans with standardized heat pain stimulation in between, and peripheral blood transcriptomic analysis. The activity and connectivity of brain regions, especially the somatosensory cortex and the posterior cingulate cortex, one of the main hubs of the default mode network (DMN), showed significant alterations in D2T RA. Furthermore, acute pain stimulation influenced connectivity patterns of D2T patients differently compared to non-D2T patients and HCs. These results are in line with the psychological profiles of D2T patients characterized by cognitive, coping, and emotional dysregulations as well as altered pain processing. Transcriptomic analysis identified mediators, pathways, and signaling mechanisms such as neuregulin 1 (NRG1) and type I interferon signaling associated with neuroinflammation and synaptic plasticity. Our findings identify central nervous system (CNS) alterations as a meaningful contributor to the D2T RA phenotype, helping to explain persistent symptom burden beyond inflammation. These characteristic neuroimmune signatures support multidisciplinary, personalized interventions that target CNS processes alongside inflammation control to improve outcomes.

title: Transplantation of directly converted HDF-iNSC to the scala tympani of the cochlea increases neural structure and central auditory connection in an auditory neuropathy animal model.
abstract: Cochlear implants (CIs) provide effective rehabilitation for severe-to-profound hearing loss, yet their success is limited by secondary degeneration of auditory neurons. Direct transdifferentiation, which enables lineage conversion of somatic cells into neural stem cells without a pluripotent stage, offers advantages over induced pluripotent stem cells by reducing tumorigenic risk, shortening reprogramming time, and producing expandable, patient-specific cells for autologous therapy. Oct4 is a critical factor for establishing pluripotency, but it is not required for direct reprogramming. Inclusion of Oct4 can enhance reprogramming efficiency and induce a more 'plastic' cellular state, which may facilitate improved integration and functional adaptation following transplantation into the target organ. Induced neural stem cells (iNSCs) were generated from human dermal fibroblasts. We generated iNSCs by transducing the exogenous Oct4 protein in combination with Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc. The properties of these iNSCs were characterized, and their therapeutic potential was evaluated following transplantation in an animal model of auditory neuropathy. Histologic and functional assessment were performed. Immunostaining and flow cytometry results showed that human iNSCs express Nestin, Sox2, and Pax6. Constitutive expression of SKM and transient Oct4 priming induced iNSCs from HDFs under NSC-permissive culture conditions. Isolated iNSCs had similar morphological features and expression markers as control human NSCs. Transplanted human iNSCs improved cochlear cellular integrity, particularly by enhancing neural structures including neurons and nerve fibers. Although peripheral synaptic connections were not restored, synaptic marker toward the central auditory pathway was significantly increased. eABR responses showed statistically higher response in iNSC transplanted animals. Direct transdifferentiation provides an efficient strategy to generate autologous iNSCs capable of preserving and repairing auditory neural structures. By improving neural health, this approach has the potential to enhance CI performance, expand candidacy to patients with long-term hearing loss, and establish a novel regenerative avenue for functional hearing restoration.

title: Recreational cannabis use in hemodialysis patients: prevalence, chronic pain profile and impact on quality of life.
abstract: Morocco is one of the world's leading suppliers of cannabis, primarily cultivated in its northern region. Smoked cannabis has been reported in the literature to relieve suffering. Pain is a prevalent symptom in hemodialysis patients, leading to decreased quality of life. Therefore, this study aims to determine the prevalence of smoking cannabis in male patients undergoing hemodialysis and to explore the sociodemographic, biological and chronic pain characteristics, and quality of life between users of recreational cannabis and non-users. A total of 186 male patients on hemodialysis were recruited from four dialysis centers in the northern Morocco region. The Numeric Rating scale was used to assess pain severity and the Short-Form 36 (SF-36) questionnaire was adopted to evaluate the quality of life. The Brief Pain Inventory was used to locate the painful sites. Data collection utilized medical files and a structured questionnaire including sociodemographic, clinical and dialysis-related variables. The prevalence of cannabis use was 18.2%. Patients in rural areas and current tobacco smokers use more cannabis. Compared to the non-smokers' group, the smokers' group had less chronic pain (p = 0.002) and lower pain severity (p = 0.006). For the quality of life, significantly higher mean scores in general health, bodily pain and vitality domains (p = 0.02), (p < 0.001) and (p = 0.009) respectively, and increased physical component summary (p = 0.003). Furthermore, cannabis smokers were more Vitamin D deficient (p = 0.009) and had a higher serum concentration of hemoglobin (p = 0.005) compared to non-smokers. Cannabis smokers were predominantly from rural areas, had a history of tobacco use and were less likely to suffer from chronic pain than non-smokers. The smoker's group had low pain severity and better quality of life compared to non-smokers. However, more research is needed to investigate the relationship of frequency, quantity and quality of cannabis on efficiency and reduction of chronic pain in patients treated by hemodialysis.

title: Strain-specific morphology and CNS propagation of template-directed SOD1 aggregation following peripheral nerve inoculation.
abstract: Accumulation of misfolded SOD1 protein into intracellular aggregates, in the spinal cord (SpC) and brainstem, is a hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis caused by mutations in the SOD1 gene (SOD1-ALS). Two distinct aggregate conformations, denoted strain A and strain B, were identified in the CNS of SOD1G85R and SOD1D90A transgenic (Tg) ALS mouse models, respectively. Both strains transmit templated SOD1 aggregation and ALS-like disease in Tg mouse models when inoculated into the SpC, whereas muscle or intraperitoneal inoculations, of up to 300 times more inoculate, did not. Here, we used strain A and strain B aggregate seeds, prepared from SpCs of the Tg mice, to investigate strain-specific differences in transmission of templated aggregation and ALS phenotype via a peripheral nerve. We show that both strains can transmit templated aggregation to the CNS via the sciatic nerve in SOD1G85R Tg mice. Strain A resulted in shorter time to disease onset and earlier end-stage disease compared to strain B, and these strain-specific differences were accentuated in the sciatic nerve inoculation model compared to direct SpC inoculations. To further analyse the differences between strain A and strain B, we developed an immunohistochemical method that distinguishes the two SOD1 aggregate strains in tissue sections. This method revealed that strain B adopts an elongated, skein-like morphology, whereas strain A aggregates appear as accumulations of rounded, bead-like structures. These findings suggest that SOD1 aggregates forming in a peripheral nerve might transmit disease to the CNS and that different SOD1 aggregate strains can influence disease onset and progression. Our results warrant further exploratory studies of SOD1 aggregate conformations and their potential role in the manifestation of SOD1 mutant-specific disease phenotypes.

title: Non-electrophilic TRPA1 modulator MNP-021 protects neuronal and glial function from diabetes-associated glucotoxicity and neuroinflammation.
abstract: Diabetes-associated neurodegeneration is amplified by methylglyoxal (MGO)-driven dicarbonyl stress linking hyperglycemia to neuronal insulin resistance and maladaptive neuroinflammation. We tested the neuroprotective activity of MNP-021, a non-electrophilic transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) modulator, in neurons and glial cells in vitro. SH-SY5Y neurons were pretreated with MNP-021 and challenged with MGO, then profiled by high-content imaging, RNA-seq, Seahorse Oxygen Consumption Rate (OCR) and Extracellular Acidification Rate (ECAR), glycolytic stress assays, and immunoblotting for AKT, ERK, and cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB). In an additional sustained glucotoxicity paradigm, differentiated SH-SY5Y cells were exposed to high glucose for 7 days and viability was assessed by LIVE/DEAD™ high-content imaging. HMC3 glial cells were treated with MNP-021, exposed to Lipopolysaccharide (LPS), Tumor Necrosis Factor-α (TNF-α) or Aβ(25-35), and tested for viability and inflammatory markers by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) and RT-qPCR. MGO increased nucleus-to-cytoplasm area ratio by 49% and dysregulated glucose handling, increasing 2-(N-(7-Nitrobenz-2-oxa-1,3-diazol-4-yl)Amino)-2-Deoxyglucose (2-NBDG) uptake by ~ 25%, with GLUT1/GLUT4 membrane redistribution; MNP-021 normalized morphology, glucose uptake, and transporter localization without cytotoxicity up to 10 µM. RNA-seq identified 754 MGO-deregulated genes, including ISR/metabolic nodes such as glucokinase (GCK), Sestrin-2 (SESN2), phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH), Phosphoserine Aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1), phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 2 (PCK2); MNP-021 buffered stress-induced transcription with limited baseline effects, modulated mitochondrial morphology and redox-associated fluorescence while preserving overall respiratory flux and blunting stress-evoked compensatory glycolysis. MNP-021 restored pro-survival signaling (pAKT/pERK and nuclear pCREB), including insulin responsiveness during MGO exposure. In a sustained high-glucose model, MNP-021 reduced the high-glucose-associated increase in cell death, extending its protective effects beyond the acute MGO paradigm. MNP-021 reduced Interleukine-6 (IL-6)/TNF-α release while increasing Interleukine-10 (IL-10) and Arginase 1 (ARG1) (~ 1.9-fold vs. LPS/TNF-α) in HMC3 glial cells, shifting them toward a pro-resolving IL-10/ARG1 program with reduced amyloid β-peptide 25-35 (Aβ(25-35))-evoked cytokine release and Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) remaining very low (≤ 10 pg/mL) and not significantly increased in this system. MNP-021 coordinates transcriptomic restraint, transporter-level glucose handling, mitochondrial resilience, and pro-survival/pro-resolving signaling in neuron-microglia cell models. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of MNP-021 in dicarbonyl-linked neuro-metabolic stress and provide pharmacological evidence consistent with a TRPA1-linked component of its activity.

title: Target-area dosimetry-guided photobiomodulation improves pathology and cognitive function in APPswe/PS1dE9 mice.
abstract: Photobiomodulation (PBM) has shown potential in Alzheimer's disease (AD) models, but substantial heterogeneity in irradiation parameters and the lack of intracerebral dose quantification have limited reproducibility and mechanistic interpretation. In transcranial PBM, surface power density does not reliably reflect energy delivery to brain targets due to wavelength-dependent tissue attenuation. We developed a target-area dosimetry- guided PBM framework by integrating Monte Carlo-based light transport modeling with inverse calibration for selected representative wavelength-target conditions. Based on these simulations, inverse calibration was performed for selected representative wavelength-target combinations, with 810 nm irradiation optimized for PFC-directed PBM and 1060 nm, 40 Hz pulsed irradiation optimized for HIPP-directed PBM. APPswe/PS1dE9 mice received region-oriented and comparative PBM treatments, followed by behavioral, pathological, and electrophysiological assessments. Monte Carlo simulations revealed marked wavelength-dependent differences in intracerebral light distribution under identical surface irradiation. Inverse calibration supported the selection of region-specific irradiation parameters and highlighted the need to consider target-area light exposure rather than surface power alone. Among the tested irradiation conditions, PBM improved spatial learning and memory and modulated amyloid burden, neuroinflammatory responses, synaptic markers, and neural network activity. Among these treatments, combined hippocampal irradiation with 810 nm and 1060 nm light produced the most consistent overall responses, while 810 nm PFC irradiation also showed beneficial effects across several outcome measures. These findings support target-area dosimetry as an important physical consideration for the design and interpretation of region-oriented PBM protocols in AD models. By integrating intracerebral light propagation modeling with biological evaluation, this study provides a methodological framework for improving PBM parameter selection and guiding future optimization of transcranial PBM interventions.

title: DNA methylation of silencer-annotated regions at the MGMT locus in the context of promoter and enhancer methylation in glioblastoma and melanoma brain metastases.
abstract: MGMT promoter methylation is a well-established biomarker in glioblastoma, its relevance in melanoma brain metastases remains controversial. Recent studies indicate that methylation of MGMT enhancers contributes to MGMT regulation, whereas the role of silencer methylation has not yet been investigated. DNA methylation of 52 CpG sites was analyzed in regions annotated as potential silencers located in the promoter, intronic, and upstream regions of MGMT. These regions were selected based on genomic annotations and their genomic proximity to MGMT, encompassing sites to approximately 1.5 Mb upstream, without experimental validation of direct regulatory activity. Analyses were performed in glioblastoma and melanoma brain metastases using in-house developed assays based on bisulfite conversion, PCR amplification of target regions, and pyrosequencing. By integrating previously published promoter and enhancer methylation data, a DNA methylation landscape of MGMT regulatory elements was established. Associations between CpG methylation and MGMT protein expression, overall survival, patient age, and sex were evaluated. The degree of methylation strongly depended on the genomic location of the respective regulatory element. Both shared and tumor-type-specific methylation patterns were observed in glioblastoma and melanoma brain metastases. Promoter-associated CpGs and selected intronic silencer-annotated regions showed associations with MGMT protein expression. In glioblastoma, several promoter-associated CpGs were associated with overall survival, whereas sex-specific and age-related effects were absent. DNA methylation of MGMT regulatory elements is highly CpG-specific. CpG-resolved analyses reveal a complex epigenetic landscape across the MGMT locus and highlight substantial regional heterogeneity. These findings suggest that extending methylation analyses beyond the classical promoter region provides additional insights into MGMT-associated epigenetic variation and its potentical clinical associations.

title: Psychometric properties of the Farsi version of the Night Eating Disorder Questionnaire.
abstract: This study assesses the factor structure and psychometric properties of Farsi version of Night Eating Questionnaire. In this cross-sectional study, we randomly selected 155 people referred to Shafa hospital and private psychiatry clinic in Rasht City, Iran. After translation to Farsi and back-translation to English, the face and content validity of NEQ Farsi version were evaluated using the opinions of a panel of experts and calculating the content validity ratio and content validity index. Then, the construct validity was evaluated by Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), the Cronbach α coefficient was used for assessing internal consistency and the Intra class Correlation Coefficient (ICC) was used for assessing test-retest reliability. The mean age of participants was 41.1 ± 12.9 Years. The CFA results showed that the four-factor model had a good fit. Cronbach's alpha showed an overall coefficient of 0.72. Spearman's correlation coefficient was 0.97 and the intra-class correlation coefficient was 0.99 (95% CI 0.97-0.99), indicating a satisfactory level of test-retest reliability. The Farsi version of the NEQ has acceptable psychometric properties for the Farsi language and Iranian culture, to be used as a valid and reliable tool in future research, care, and therapeutic activities.

title: The journey of numbers from attention to motor processing: an embodied account of neural response to number magnitudes.
abstract: Embodied cognition suggests numbers are linked to physical actions and sensory experiences. Additionally, sensory processing, thoughts or actions are modulated by attentional shifts/control. This study investigates how learned motor associations in individuals (finger-counting habits) shape brain responses to digit symbols. We examined how covert attention to motor associations influences neural responses during passive viewing of symbolic numbers, using event-related potentials (ERPs) and time-frequency analysis. We examined whether the P2 component, linked to attentional processing, correlates with motor habits and alpha wave activity. Results showed stronger P2 component when number-hand associations aligned, with no significant alpha wave changes was observed. Right-starters exhibited enhanced attention and number processing, with higher P3 amplitudes and faster responses for all digits. Taken together, these findings provide preliminary support for the idea that attention to learned motor associations may influence neural responses to numerical information. We discuss these findings within our proposed theoretical framework termed Feature-based Attention to Learned Motor (FALM) processing.

title: Endothelial KLK10 maintains blood-brain barrier integrity and mitigates ischemic stroke by limiting the cGAS-STING pathway.
abstract: Despite significant advances in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) reperfusion therapies, blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction continues to drive poor clinical outcomes. While endogenous vascular protective mechanisms remain incompletely characterized, kallikrein-related peptidase 10 (KLK10) - a serine protease with unexplored neurovascular functions - represents a promising candidate for BBB regulation. We employed a translational strategy to characterize KLK10 expression in plasma samples from 182 AIS patients, human postmortem stroke brain tissues, and a mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). We elucidated KLK10's functional mechanisms through studies using genetic knockout mice, endothelial-specific KLK10 knockdown models, recombinant KLK10 (rKLK10) administration, KLK10 overexpression in cultured brain endothelial cells (BECs), pharmacological inhibition, and primary BEC cultures. We demonstrate that KLK10 is markedly upregulated in both human postmortem stroke brain tissues and MCAO mouse brains, with predominant expression in cerebrovascular endothelial cells. Clinically, plasma KLK10 levels in AIS patients correlate with both disease severity and 3-month prognosis. Functional studies reveal that KLK10 protects against brain injury and BBB disruption by suppressing endothelial inflammatory cell adhesion molecules, and preserving junctional integrity. Mechanistically, KLK10 may exert its protective effects by limiting the cerebrovascular endothelial cyclic GMP-AMP synthase - stimulator of interferon genes - nuclear factor kappa B (cGAS-STING-NF-κB) pathway, a previously unrecognized regulatory mechanism in stroke-associated endothelial dysfunction. Our study suggests that KLK10 may serve as a candidate prognostic indicator and potential therapeutic target for AIS, exerting its protective effects via maintaining BBB integrity and via the novel regulation of the cerebrovascular cGAS-STING-NF-κB pathway, thereby offering new insights for vascular protection in stroke and related neuroinflammatory conditions.

title: Large-scale compound screening reveals sensitivities to SM1-71, HDACs/mTOR Inhibitor 1, BGT226, and ON013100 in glioma.
abstract: Gliomas, particularly glioblastomas (GBM), are the most aggressive primary brain tumors with poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options. Resistance to temozolomide and high tumor invasiveness underscore the urgent need for novel therapeutic agents. We performed a large-scale screening of 1,460 small-molecule compounds using three human glioma cell lines (U251, LN229, and A172) to identify candidate anti-glioma agents. Four compounds with limited prior investigation in gliomas-SM1-71 (TAK1 inhibitor), HDACs/mTOR Inhibitor 1, BGT226 (PI3K/mTOR inhibitor), and ON013100 (mitotic inhibitor)-were selected for detailed in vitro and in vivo evaluation. In vitro assays included cell viability (CCK-8), cell cycle analysis, apoptosis, migration, and invasion assays. In vivo efficacy was assessed in a subcutaneous xenograft mouse model. SM1-71, HDACs/mTOR Inhibitor 1, BGT226, and ON013100 significantly inhibited glioma cell proliferation, induced G2-phase cell cycle arrest, and promoted apoptosis. All four compounds suppressed glioma cell migration and invasion in vitro. In the xenograft model, SM1-71 and ON013100 showed the most pronounced tumor growth inhibition (~ 75% reduction), whereas BGT226 and HDACs/mTOR Inhibitor 1 exhibited moderate effects. Ki-67 immunostaining confirmed decreased tumor cell proliferation. No significant body weight loss was observed, although isolated mortality indicated the need for further toxicity evaluation. This study identifies four promising anti-glioma compounds with potent in vitro and in vivo activity, particularly SM1-71 and ON013100. These findings support further preclinical investigation of these compounds, particularly with respect to pharmacokinetics, blood-brain barrier penetration, toxicity, and combination with standard therapies.

title: MRgFUS-enabled nanogel platform for synergstic chemo-immunotherapy in glioblastoma.
abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with poor prognosis and limited responsiveness to temozolomide (TMZ)-based chemoradiotherapy. Treatment remains hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB), blood-brain tumor barrier (BBTB), acquired TMZ resistance, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. To overcome these challenges, we developed a multifunctional nanogel platform for co-delivering TMZ and PD-L1-targeting siRNA. TMZ not only exerts direct cytotoxicity against GBM cells but also induces immunogenic cell death (ICD), promoting the release of damage-associated molecular patterns and tumor-associated antigens for antitumor immune activation. Meanwhile, siRNA-mediated PD-L1 silencing alleviates immune evasion and potentiates T-cell-mediated antitumor responses. Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) was employed to locally disrupt the BBB/BBTB and enhance nanogel penetration. Ultrasmall iron oxide nanoparticles (USIO) provided T1-weighted MRI contrast for real-time monitoring of nanogel distribution and tumor targeting. Distinct from conventional FUS-nanoparticle platforms, this MRgFUS-guided theranostic nanogel integrates TMZ-based chemotherapy, TMZ-induced ICD, siRNA-mediated PD-L1 silencing, and MRI-traceable delivery into a single platform, enabling image-guided, spatiotemporally precise chemo-immunotherapy for glioblastoma.

title: Factors associated with the use of UK emergency services in children and young people with intellectual developmental disabilities.
