authors: van den Bree Marianne B M
abstract: Children and young people (CYP) with intellectual developmental disabilities (IDD) experience substantial health needs and higher healthcare utilisation compared with the general paediatric population. However, factors affecting the emergency healthcare use among children with IDD of genetic aetiology remain poorly understood. This study aimed to examine demographic, socioeconomic, behavioural, genetic, and clinical factors of emergency service use among CYP with IDD in England. This retrospective cohort study used linked administrative healthcare data from Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) emergency service records obtained from National Health Service (NHS) England. Participants were CYP aged between 4 and 15.5 years with confirmed pathogenic genetic variants associated with IDD identified via NHS medical genetic clinics. The outcome was the yearly emergency service use rate, calculated as the total number of lifetime emergency visits divided by age (years). Independent variables included demographic and socioeconomic factors, genetic characteristics, region of residence, adaptive functioning, behavioural and emotional adjustment, prosocial behaviour, general health status, and system-specific medical conditions. Primary caregivers completed questionnaires and provided information regarding the child's medical history and demographic information. The average emergency attendance rate in this cohort was 0.73 visits per annum, which was much higher than that among children in the same age range from the general population. Emergency services were used more by younger IDD children with poorer adaptive functioning, more externalising and less prosocial behaviour, as well as those with complex multisystem conditions. Frequent attendance was associated with high rates of medical comorbidities especially seizures and respiratory problems. Regional differences were found with relatively higher usage in London and the North East of England. Attendance rates were not influenced by sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic deprivation, genetic variant type or inheritance status. This novel study demonstrated emergency healthcare utilisation among CYP with IDD of known genetic aetiology in England was primarily associated with clinical complexity, functional impairment, and younger age rather than socioeconomic or genetic factors. Their vulnerability to multisystem morbidity as well as regional disparities highlight the need for improved coordinated care and targeted service planning to reduce emergency healthcare dependence among children with disabilities.

title: Markers of blood-brain barrier and intestinal mucosal barrier in insomnia disorder: an observational study linking wake-promoting neurotransmitters to sleep efficiency.
abstract: The present study aimed to investigate the alterations in wake-promoting neurotransmitters (histamine and orexin-A) and markers of blood-brain barrier and intestinal mucosal barrier including zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1), claudin-5, zonulin, and S100 calcium-binding protein B (S100β) in insomnia disorder (ID). Additionally, we examined the correlations between these neurotransmitters and barrier markers, and explored their combined associations with sleep parameters. This study enrolled 54 ID patients and 45 healthy controls. The demographic and clinical characteristics of all participants were investigated, and participants underwent overnight polysomnography. Serum levels of wake-promoting neurotransmitters and barrier markers were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Spearman's correlation analysis was conducted to explore the associations between these serum biomarkers and sleep parameters, as well as between the neurotransmitters and barrier markers. Furthermore, mediation analysis was performed to examine whether barrier markers mediated the relationship between wake-promoting neurotransmitters and sleep parameters. Levels of peripheral wake-promoting neurotransmitters (histamine and orexin-A) and barrier markers (zonulin, S100β, ZO-1, and claudin-5) were elevated in the ID group (all p < 0.001). Additionally, sleep efficiency was positively correlated with histamine levels (r = 0.57), negatively correlated with orexin-A levels (r = -0.62), and positively correlated with ZO-1 levels (r = 0.56) in ID patients. Moreover, histamine levels showed positive correlations with claudin-5 (r = 0.37) and ZO-1 (r = 0.31), and a negative correlation with S100β (r = -0.33). Additionally, orexin-A was negatively correlated with claudin-5 levels (r = -0.46). Furthermore, ZO-1 showed a statistical mediation effect in the associations between histamine and sleep efficiency (p = 0.006) as well as between orexin-A and sleep efficiency (p = 0.012), consistent with a potential indirect pathway. This study observed dysregulation of peripheral wake-promoting neurotransmitters along with markers of blood-brain barrier and intestinal mucosal barrier in ID patients. Notably, ZO-1 showed a statistical mediation effect in the associations between these neurotransmitters and sleep efficiency, though causality cannot be inferred from the cross-sectional design. These clinical findings provide preliminary insights into the molecular features associated with ID and may inform directions for future mechanistic research. Further studies are needed to fully elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

title: Predictive factors of hospital case-fatality in patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.
abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is the most lethal subtype of stroke, accounting for approximately 20% of all stroke cases, and has a high early mortality rate, largely because effective acute treatments are limited compared with ischemic stroke. Identifying reliable predictors of hospital case-fatality is essential for risk stratification and treatment optimization. This retrospective analytic observational hospital-based study (April 2024 to June 2025, Imam Reza Hospital) included 90 patients with ICH (40 deceased, 50 survivors). We analyzed demographic information, clinical and laboratory parameters, comorbidities, hemorrhage characteristics, and the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) as a measure of functional disability. The primary outcome was hospital case-fatality. All Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and mRS assessments were measured by a neurologist at two times (the first and last day of hospitalization). Multivariate analysis identified independent and significant predictors of hospital case-fatality: GCS less than 7 at admission (Odds Ratio (OR) = 5.21, 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 4.85-9.41), GCS less than 7 in the last day (OR = 5.96, 95% CI: 3.78-9.05), Hematoma volume > 25 mL (OR = 14.20, 95% CI: 11.52-32.63), intraventricular hemorrhage (OR = 8.23, 95% CI: 5.63-9.96), deep location of hematoma (OR = 5.63, 95% CI: 4.49-8.75); mRS > 3 at discharge (OR = 12.63, 95% CI: 8.41-18.30), mRS > 3 at admission (OR = 8.11, 95% CI: 7.63-11.25), and hypertension (OR = 2.22, 95% CI: 1.41-4.02). Hospital case-fatality in ICH patients is independently predicted by hematoma volume, intraventricular hemorrhage extension, deep hematoma location, impaired consciousness, high functional disability scores, and hypertension. Early and systematic assessment of these factors could improve prognostic accuracy and guide personalized clinical decision-making.

title: Bouldering-Psychotherapy for treating depression in adolescents (BooSt): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Currently, there are hardly any validated group therapy programs for depressed adolescents in Germany. A recent meta-analysis confirmed a moderate antidepressant effect of exercise in adolescents with depressive symptoms. In addition, four recent systematic reviews reported positive effects of exercise interventions on psychological well-being, mood, and quality of life in adolescents with depression or depressive symptoms. We developed a manualized behavioral-therapy-based group program involving Bouldering-Psychotherapy (BPT) for adolescents (BPT-J) based on the adult version of BPT, which has already demonstrated its efficacy. The aim of the study is to evaluate the efficacy of BPT-J. The study is designed as a randomized, controlled, prospective, longitudinal, single-blind trial with two arms (BPT-J intervention group [IG], waitlist-control group [CG]). The primary aim is to investigate the efficacy of the BPT-J group therapy for adolescents for treating depressiveness. Eligible participants are adolescents with subclinical and clinical depressive symptoms between 13 and 18 years of age. The adolescents in the CG are offered participation in an identical intervention after t1. The 10-week intervention is accompanied by four data collection points for all participants: participants and their legal guardians fill out online questionnaires at the start of therapy (t0), immediately after IG therapy (t1), after CG therapy (t2), and 12 months after finalizing the intervention (follow-up, t3). In addition, structured video interviews are conducted at t0 and t1. BooSt trial addresses the limited availability of evidence-based group interventions for adolescents with depressive symptoms in routine care. If efficacy is confirmed, BPT-J may represent a scalable, manualized, and potentially well-accepted treatment approach that could complement existing psychotherapeutic services for adolescents. Given the increasing demand and limited access to psychotherapy, the intervention may contribute to improving accessibility of mental health care. The group-based format may additionally support cost-effective implementation, reduce waiting times, facilitate peer support, and help reduce stigmatization associated with mental health treatment. Findings from the BooSt trial may further inform dissemination and implementation strategies in child and adolescent mental health care. ISRCTN, ISRCTN79659949, prospectively registered 19/02/2025, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN79659949 , URL: https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN79659949 .

title: Association between anticholinergic burden and geographic atrophy secondary to age-related macular degeneration: a case-control study.
abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of visual impairment in older adults. Given the high prevalence of polypharmacy in this population, cumulative medication effects, particularly anticholinergic burden, may represent a clinically relevant factor requiring further investigation. This study aimed to investigate the association between anticholinergic burden, overall drug burden, and geographic atrophy secondary age-related macular degeneration (GA secondary to AMD). In this case-control study, 102 participants aged 55-90 years were included. Anticholinergic burden was assessed using the Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) scale. Medications regularly used by patients for chronic conditions and continued for a minimum duration of three months were included. Drug burden was defined as polypharmacy (≥ 5 medications). Multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed adjusting for age, gender, and multimorbidity. Patients with GA secondary to AMD had a higher number of medications and a greater prevalence of both drug burden and anticholinergic burden compared to controls (p = 0.010, p = 0.039, and p = 0.046, respectively). In multivariate analysis, anticholinergic burden (OR: 2.55, 95% CI: 1.11-5.84, p = 0.026) and drug burden (OR: 3.41, 95% CI: 1.21-9.58, p = 0.017) were independently associated with GA secondary to AMD. Increased anticholinergic and overall drug burden were independently associated with GA secondary to AMD in older adults. These findings suggest a potential relationship between cumulative medication exposure and AMD. Further prospective studies are needed to determine whether this association has clinical or causal significance.

title: Editorial Expression of Concern: Drugs developed to treat diabetes, liraglutide and lixisenatide, cross the blood brain barrier and enhance neurogenesis.

Ecotype-associated structural variants across multiple locally adapted Poeciliid fishes.
abstract: Extreme environments provide powerful natural laboratories for studying evolutionary convergence across taxa. While convergent phenotypes frequently evolve in response to similar selective pressures, consistent molecular signatures at the nucleotide level are often elusive, potentially due to overlooked genetic variants such as structural variants. Here, we leverage recent advances in long-read sequencing and pangenome approaches to investigate the role of structural variants in repeated adaptation to toxic springs rich in hydrogen sulfide (H2S) across multiple independently evolved populations within the Poecilia mexicana species complex. We identified more than 99,000 structural variants over 50 base pairs in length, including insertions, deletions, duplications and inversions, using complementary graph- and read-based methods. We then integrated these with population genomic data and RNA-sequencing data to detect variants in highly differentiated regions between ecotypes and assess their functional impacts. Structural variants in both coding and regulatory regions were enriched in genes involved in sulfide metabolism and ion transport, including ethe1, slc13a1, and sqor. We found ecotype-specific structural variants in promoter and intronic regions of key detoxification genes that exhibited elevated expression in H2S-adapted populations. Our findings suggest that structural variation may contribute to adaptive phenotypes and should be considered in studies of genomic convergence.

title: The effects of urapidil as an alpha receptor blocker on spinal cord ischemia-reperfusion injury in male rats.
abstract: The present experimental study was designed to evaluate the potential neuroprotective effects of urapidil during the acute phase (24 hours) of spinal cord ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model, with a focus on early functional, biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical changes. Rats were randomly assigned to four experimental groups (n = 6 per group): Control (CR), Sham (SH), Ischemia-Reperfusion (IR), and Ischemia-Reperfusion + Urapidil (IR+URA). Spinal cord ischemia was induced by infrarenal abdominal aortic clamping for 30 minutes followed by reperfusion. Urapidil was administered before ischemia and after reperfusion in the IR+URA group. Motor function was evaluated 24 hours after reperfusion using the Tarlov scoring system, and biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical analyses were performed. Data were analyzed using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by Duncan's multiple comparison test, which was selected due to its greater sensitivity in exploratory studies with small sample sizes. A p-value [Formula: see text] was considered statistically significant. Motor function was significantly impaired in the IR group compared with all other groups, whereas the IR+URA group demonstrated preserved motor performance comparable to the CR and SH groups. Urapidil administration significantly increased antioxidant activity, as reflected by elevated glutathione peroxidase levels, and reduced inflammatory markers including TNF-α and IL-1β. Histopathological and immunohistochemical findings showed marked neuronal degeneration, apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation in the IR group, which were notably attenuated by URA treatment. In this experimental spinal cord ischemia-reperfusion model, urapidil treatment was associated with improved early motor performance, increased glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activity, and reduced levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-1β during the acute reperfusion period. These changes occurred alongside favorable histopathological findings; however, given the short follow-up duration and the limited scope of apoptotic assessment, the results should be considered preliminary and interpreted as hypothesis-generating.

title: Migraine-related differences in connectivity patterns during emotional audiovisual processing revealed by functional connectivity multivariate pattern analysis.
journal: The journal of headache and pain
abstract: Migraine is a complex neurobiological disorder characterized by recurrent headache attacks accompanied by sensory, cognitive, autonomic, and affective symptoms. Migraine has been associated with alterations in visual and auditory processing, as well as increased sensitivity to sensory stimuli both during and between attacks. Migraine has also been associated with increased sensitivity to the arousal and valence of emotional stimuli, though this relationship is not well understood. The present study investigates how migraine influences large-scale network interactions during complex emotional audiovisual processing. Functional magnetic resonance imaging data was collected from 22 migraineurs and 21 healthy controls during the passive viewing of three audiovisual films (negative valence/high arousal; positive valence/high arousal; neutral valence/low arousal). Functional connectivity multivariate pattern analysis (fc-MVPA) identified distributed connectivity patterns that differentiated the groups. During the negative valence, high-arousal condition, fc-MVPA identified a cluster in the superior lateral occipital cortex within the default mode network (DMN) that exhibited greater within-network connectivity in migraineurs relative to controls. Additional clusters located in the visual and attention networks showed differential whole-brain connectivity between groups, characterized by increased cross-network coupling with the attention, control, and visual networks in the migraine group. Further significant clusters were also identified within the control and limbic networks. These findings indicate that migraine-related network connectivity differences were observed during the negative valence/high arousal film condition, but not during the positive valence/high arousal or neutral valence/low arousal conditions. Taken together, these results suggest that migraine is associated with network-level differences during more true-to-life emotional processing.

title: ARRDC4 drives Tau pathology via USP14-mediated deubiquitination and acts as a novel therapeutic target in Alzheimer's disease.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Hyperphosphorylated Tau accumulation drives neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but mechanisms linking impaired Tau ubiquitination to disease progression remain incompletely defined. We integrated Drosophila RNAi screening, human AD datasets, cellular assays, and mouse tauopathy models to evaluate arrestin domain-containing 4 (ARRDC4) in Tau pathology. ARRDC4-dependent regulation of Tau ubiquitination was examined using proteomics, proximity labeling, co-immunoprecipitation, BiFC, domain mapping, genetic suppression, and small-molecule interference. ARRDC4 was upregulated in AD-relevant human and animal datasets and correlated with Tau burden. ARRDC4 overexpression promoted Tau phosphorylation, self-association, seeded aggregation, secretion, and inflammatory activation. Mechanistically, ARRDC4 brought Tau and USP14 into proximity, suppressing Tau ubiquitination. Genetic ARRDC4 deficiency or pharmacological disruption of the ARRDC4-USP14 interface restored Tau ubiquitination and ameliorated Tau pathology, neuroinflammation, neuronal injury, and behavioral deficits across cellular, Drosophila, and mouse models. ARRDC4 is a regulator of Tau proteostasis and a potential therapeutic target for Tau-associated AD pathology.

title: Still's disease and malignancies: insights into the balance between inflammatory enhancement and immune control. Data from the International AIDA Network Still's Disease Registry.
abstract: Still's disease is an autoinflammatory condition marked by excessive activation of the innate immune system, resulting in intense and persistent systemic inflammation if left untreated. Chronic inflammation is recognized as both an initiator and promoter of carcinogenesis, although growing evidence suggests it may act against cancer development. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the cancer risk in patients with Still's disease. Data were obtained from the international Autoinflammatory Diseases Alliance (AIDA) Network registry for Still's disease. Statistical analysis included a machine learning-based approach to evaluate associations between independent variables and malignancy. A total of 626 patients with Still's disease were included, of whom 14 (2.2%) developed 15 malignant neoplasms. Patients with malignancy history exhibited higher age at disease onset and diagnosis, as well as longer duration of fever during flares. Machine learning-based analysis, including Elastic Net and Firth's penalized likelihood logistic regression, identified an association between cancer development and fever duration (relative risk = 1.002, 95% confidence interval 1.000-1.004, p = 0.01). Despite being a severe systemic inflammatory condition, Still's disease appears to be associated with a relatively modest prevalence of cancer. However, uncontrolled systemic inflammation, as reflected by prolonged fever duration, may contribute to carcinogenesis in these patients.

title: First-in-Human Phase 1b/2a Trial Shows Safety with MEK 1/2 Inhibitor EDV2209 as A Novel Treatment for Spontaneous Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
abstract: We report findings from a Phase 1/2a clinical trial (EUCT No. 2024-514590-22-00, STOP-DCI), an interventional, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple ascending-dose, first-in-human trial to determine safety and evaluate clinical outcome for the MEK 1/2 inhibitor EDV2209 in patients with severe spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). In Phase 1b (N = 11), three cohorts received a single intracerebral ventricular (ICV) bolus (8.55 µg, 17-28.5 µg). In Phase 2a (N = 16), two cohorts were given three ICV injections of 28.5 µg EDV2209 or placebo over 18 h, beginning within 8 h of SAH onset.The study found an equal distribution of adverse events between treatment and placebo with no treatment-associated safety concerns. Outcomes and mortality were as expected or better for patients with severe SAH in the patients treated with EDV2209. Pharmacokinetics were reproducibly stable in the CSF with no detectable levels of EDV2209 in plasma.Treatment with EDV2209 was considered safe and was interpreted to provide potential benefit for improving patient outcome following severe SAH. These results provide a rationale to continue with a Phase 2b / 3 study powered to determine efficacy as well as safety.

title: Italian guideline on palliative care in adult patients with grade 3/4 gliomas.
journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
abstract: The palliative and supportive care needs of adults with glioma are complex. In 2017, the European Association for Neuro-Oncology (EANO) published the guideline on palliative care (PC) in this population. To develop a clinical practice guideline for the PC of adults with CNS WHO grade 3/4 gliomas by updating and adapting the EANO guideline to the Italian context. The guideline was produced by an interdisciplinary, consumer-inclusive panel appointed by the three main Italian scientific associations for neurology, neuro-oncology and PC, following the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). The panel formulated two clinical questions, addressed by three recommendations (all based on very-low-certainty evidence) and one Good Practice Statement: (1) We suggest the use of structured communication interventions to convey diagnosis, prognosis, and/or therapeutic and care options (conditional recommendation). (2) We recommend using approaches/tools to facilitate information processing in adults with glioma with reduced decision-making capacity (strong recommendation). (3) We believe it is appropriate to monitor the emotional impact that communication can have, and to provide support to adults with glioma and their caregivers (Good Practice Statement). (4) We suggest offering adults with CNS WHO grade 3/4 glioma a healthcare model that integrates the best anti-tumor and palliative treatments through early, dynamic, interdisciplinary, and multi-professional management of emerging health needs. The integrated model should be aligned with patients' care preferences and caregivers' needs and provided throughout the whole disease trajectory and across all care settings (conditional recommendation). This guideline provides recommendations for improving communication and integrated PC for adults with glioma and their caregivers. It also provides indications for future research priorities in this population.
